CAUSE: The hang occurs after the timeout, when `bash()` waits for `reader` to finish. `asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(reader), timeout=...)` does enforce the timeout; shielding keeps `proc.communicate()` running after the timeout. In `app/harness/tools.py`, the timeout handler calls `_kill_proc(proc)` and then unconditionally awaits `reader`. If a child escapes the process group but inherits stdout, killing the group does not close the pipe, so `communicate()` never finishes and the harness call hangs.

Evidence: I reproduced it with `setsid sleep 20 & echo ready` and a one-second tool timeout; the call was still pending after five seconds. The cleanup path is in `app/bg_jobs.py`: `_cleanup_pidfd_group()` signals the owned process group, which cannot kill a child that has moved to another session.

Recommended fix: bound the post-kill drain, then cancel and reap the reader if the pipe remains open. Also ensure cancellation cleanup cannot wait indefinitely on inherited pipe handles.
